note:
The 1901 census round for Clare Valley, Park Valley, Huntingdon Drive, Park Row, Park Terrace and Newcastle Drive - Brewhouse Yard & Standard Hill, Castle ward, pages 9 to 17, schedules 47 to 103.

**This closes three of the six blocks the gap report found**: Park Valley, Park Terrace and Newcastle Drive, each of which the record held in 1891 and again in 1911 or 1921 but not in between.

**It is NOT named people_*.json on purpose**, so the importer never reads it. It is a transcription waiting to be checked. A reading I am unsure of carries [?].

Park Valley and Park Terrace are numbered on the page, so those households can be filed to houses rather than left on the unfiled queue. Huntingdon Drive and Park Row are not numbered and cannot be.

**PELHAM TERRACE IS NEWCASTLE DRIVE.** Pages 18 and 19 are headed Pelham Terrace, which is the upper end of the same street under its older name. A. Hagues's rule applies: **Newcastle Drive number = 39 minus the Pelham Terrace number**, fixed by the Fosters at 12 Pelham Terrace = 27 Newcastle Drive. Each converted number is given as newcastle_drive_number. See [[newcastle-drive-pelham-terrace-numbers]].

**And it puts the Fosters back where they belong.** William Foster, cabinet maker, is at 12 Pelham Terrace in 1901 - which is 27 Newcastle Drive, the house the record already holds him at in 1891 and his widow Mary at in 1921. They never moved. That fills the gap at #221 with the same family on both sides of it.
source: 1901 census - transcribed by Claude from the enumerator's pages supplied by A. Hagues

households.note: The record already holds this household in full and knows the house: Elmsdale, placed on Clare Valley / Tattershall Drive by Wright's Directory. Arthur Lewis (#3359) and Margaret (#3360) carry 1891 there as well.

**CONFIRMED AGAINST THE PUBLISHED INDEX, AND THE RECORD IS WRONG.** The index gives this household at 5 Park Terrace exactly as read here - Herbert F Lancashire, head, single, 31, manager of a hosiery mill; Edith H Taylor, sister, widow, 33; Elizabeth Gordon, servant, widow, 36, cook, born Yorkshire.

The record instead carries 1901 rows for #51 and #401 at **Castlethorpe, Newcastle Circus**. Neither has a source and Edith's has no age, and the household there is only two people where the page gives three. His **1911** row at Castlethorpe is sound, so the 1901 pair was very probably worked backwards from it. **He moved between the two censuses**, and the 1901 rows want moving to #245.

Confirmed against the published index: Herbert Lancashire, widower, 62, hosiery manufacturer, born Sandiacre; Walter H, son, 26, mechanical engineer; Elizabeth, sister, single, 53, born Osmaston; H Anna Smith, cook, 39, born Burton; Ada Hollis, 17, housekeeper. The index gives the cook's forename as **H Anna**, which this transcription now follows.

Father at 8 and son at 5 - two Lancashire households three doors apart, both in hosiery.
